section: 7. differential attention: subtract the noise
text: How it works (Ye et al., Microsoft Research and Tsinghua, arXiv 2410.05258 ): split each head's query and key into two halves, compute two attention maps, and subtract one from the other: DiffAttn(X) = ( softmax(Q 1 K 1 T /√d) − λ · softmax(Q 2 K 2 T /√d) ) V λ learned per layer: exp(λ q1 · λ k1 ) − exp(λ q2 · λ k2 ) + λ init , with λ init = 0.8 − 0.6 exp(−0.3 (l − 1)) after a per-head RMSNorm ("GroupNorm applies normalization to each head independently") times (1 − λ init ) Noise common to both maps cancels, like a differential amplifier; the weights can now be negative. authors' results : "Diff Transformer requires only about 65% of model size or training tokens" to match a Transformer (a 6.8B DIFF matches an 11B Transformer; 160B tokens match 251B); 3B models on 350B tokens average 56.2 against 55.4 zero-shot and 58.0 against 56.4 five-shot (Table 8); multi-needle retrieval at 4K with 6 needles 0.85 against 0.55 (Table 2); attention on the answer span 0.27 against 0.03, on noise 0.01 against 0.51 (Table 3); largest attention logit 38.8 against 318.0 (Table 5).
